The user wants to convert 10 dollars to euros and then make a deposit of 10 dollars into their local bank account with account number 987654. The user says "make a 10 dollar deposit" but they also want to convert 10 dollars to euros. Possibly they want to deposit 10 dollars? Or deposit the converted amount? The user says "convert 10 dollars to Euros and make a 10 dollar deposit". That seems contradictory: if you convert 10 dollars to euros, you get some euros. Then making a 10 dollar deposit would be depositing 10 dollars, not the euros. But maybe they want to deposit the converted euros? The user might have mis-specified. Let's interpret: They want to convert 10 dollars to euros, then deposit the resulting euros into their local bank account. But the deposit amount is 10 dollars? Actually, they say "make a 10 dollar deposit". So maybe they want to deposit 10 dollars into their local bank account. But why convert 10 dollars to euros? Maybe they want to deposit 10 dollars but first convert it to euros? That doesn't make sense. Alternatively, they want to convert 10 dollars to euros, then deposit the equivalent euros into their local bank account. But the deposit amount is 10 dollars? That is ambiguous.

We can ask clarifying question: "Do you want to deposit the converted euros or the original 10 dollars?" But we can't ask clarifying question because we have to produce an answer. We could interpret as: convert 10 dollars to euros, then deposit the resulting euros into the account. But the deposit amount is 10 dollars? That is contradictory. We can ask clarifying question. But the instructions say we should not ask clarifying question unless necessary. But here it's ambiguous. We can ask clarifying question. But the user specifically said "make a 10 dollar deposit". So maybe they want to deposit 10 dollars. But then why convert 10 dollars to euros? Possibly they want to convert 10 dollars to euros for some other purpose, but deposit 10 dollars into their local bank account. So we can do two separate actions: convert 10 dollars to euros, then deposit 10 dollars into account 987654. That seems plausible. So we will call the currency conversion function with amount=10, from_currency="USD", to_currency="EUR". Then we will call the banking_service function with account_id="987654", amount=10. We'll do them sequentially. The user didn't specify the target currency code. We'll assume "EUR" for euros. We'll use "USD" for US dollars. We'll proceed.
